sources.title: The Duration of the Repeated-Bout Effect After Eccentric Exercise
sources.authors: Theodorou AA, Margaritelis NV, Karyofyllidou AV, Christodoulou F, Jamurtas AZ, et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 48 recreationally active young men without muscle-damaging exercise in the prior 6 months; four independent groups repeating the same maximal eccentric knee-extensor bout (5 x 15 at 60 deg/s) after 3, 6, 9 or 12 weeks; outcomes on days 2 and 4.
sources.findings: The prior bout attenuated damage markers at 3 and 6 weeks across most outcomes, partly at 9 weeks (day 2), and not at 12 weeks; the protection comes from a prior bout of the same exercise.
sources.locator: Europe PMC full-text XML read this session through WebFetch (first 100,000 of 126,036 characters): Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion (limitations).
limitations: Young men, one muscle group, a maximal laboratory protocol far heavier than a 1-set establishment dose; days 2 and 4 only.
counterevidence: A single low-volume set at RIR 3-4 is unlikely to cause the damage of a maximal eccentric bout.
